name: Konbaung dynasty
native: ကုန်းဘောင်ခေတ်

successors.name: Kingdom of Burma (Konbaung dynasty)
successors.text: the Cliopatria row 'Burma' (1820-1884): the same Konbaung state under Bagyidaw

ledger.x: 29 February 1752: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty at Shwebo.
20 April 1752: the Konbaung-Hanthawaddy War begins.
1753: Upper Burma but Ava is Konbaung.
1754: the nearer Shan states return to Burma.
1754: Upper Burma is secure.
3 January 1754: Hsinbyushin retakes Ava.
January 1755: the invasion of Lower Burma.
5 May 1755: the Irrawaddy Delta and Dagon fall.
26 July 1756: Syriam falls and French involvement ends.
6 May 1757: Pegu falls.

6 May 1757: the Konbaung-Hanthawaddy War ends in a 'Decisive Konbaung victory'; the last king of Hanthawaddy was executed in 1774 and Mon revolts followed in 1758, 1762, 1774, 1783, 1792 and 1824-1826.
1759: war with Siam over the Tenasserim coast.
1758-59: Alaungpaya brings the farther Shan states and the Kachin hills back under Burmese authority.
ledger.cp: Farther Shan states and northern Kachin

ledger.x: 1760: upper Tenasserim is Burmese.
1760: the first Burmese-Siamese war ends with Alaungpaya's death; Ayutthaya is not taken.
1760: the capital moves from Shwebo to Sagaing.
1762: the conquest of Lan Na begins.
Late 1763: Tavoy rises and returns to Siam.
August 1763: Chiang Mai falls to the Burmese.
1763: Lan Na is Burmese; the lords of Lan Na serve as Burmese governors until the Siamese take Chiang Mai in January 1775.
1765: the capital moves from Sagaing to Ava.
January 1765: Tenasserim.
March 1765: Luang Prabang becomes a Burmese vassal.
March 1765: Vientiane becomes a Burmese vassal.
23 August 1765: the Burmese invasion of Siam.
December 1765: the first Qing invasion.
7 April 1767: Ayutthaya falls and the Burmese hold the ruins.

7 April 1767: the Burmese-Siamese War of 1765-1767 ends with the fall of Ayutthaya; Hsinbyushin had ordered his besiegers in January 1767 'to finish up the conquest of Ayutthaya' so he could face the Qing.
November 1767: Taksin retakes the capital region.
13 December 1769: the Treaty of Kaungton ends the Sino-Burmese War.
January 1775: the Siamese take Chiang Mai.
January 1775: Lampang and Lamphun pass to Thonburi.
October 1775: the Burmese invade northern Siam.
August 1776: the Burmese leave Siam.
1778: Luang Prabang passes under Siam.
1779: Vientiane passes from Burma to Siam.
1783: Bodawpaya moves the capital to Amarapura.
2 December 1784: the invasion of Arakan begins.
2 January 1785: Mrauk U falls and Arakan is annexed.
January 1785: the Arakan campaign ends with the capture of Mrauk U; the Burmese invasions of Siam in 1785 and 1786 'failed' and moved no border.
1792: Tavoy and Mergui pass to Siam.
16 January 1794: the Burmese retake Tavoy.
1804: Chiang Saen falls to Chiang Mai.
1814: Bodawpaya annexes Manipur.
1817: Assam. 'He acquired Manipur in 1814 and Assam in 1817'; Burma ceded Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim to Britain in 1826 (First Anglo-Burmese War).
1819: Cliopatria's 'Konbaung Dynasty' row ends with Bodawpaya and the state continues as the 'Burma' row; the dynasty itself reigned until 29 November 1885.

wars.name: Konbaung-Hanthawaddy War
wars.outcome: Decisive Konbaung victory: Ava retaken on 3 January 1754, Dagon and the delta in May 1755, Syriam on 26 July 1756, Pegu on 6 May 1757; Lower Burma annexed down to upper Tenasserim.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1759-1760)
wars.outcome: The Konbaung armies seized the upper Tenasserim coast; Ayutthaya was not taken.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1765-1767)
wars.outcome: Burmese victory: Tenasserim lost to Burma in 1765, Lan Na held from August 1763, Luang Prabang and Vientiane vassals from March 1765, Ayutthaya fell on 7 April 1767; Taksin retook the Chao Phraya region in November 1767.

wars.name: Sino-Burmese War (1765-1769)
wars.outcome: Burmese victory in four Qing invasions; Treaty of Kaungton, 13 December 1769.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1775-1776)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Chiang Mai taken by the Siamese in January 1775; the Burmese invaded Northern Siam in October 1775, took Sukhothai and Phitsanulok and left by August 1776.

wars.name: Konbaung conquest of Arakan
wars.outcome: Burmese victory: Mrauk U captured on 2 January 1785 and Arakan annexed.

wars.name: Burmese invasions of Siam (1785-1786)
wars.outcome: The Burmese invasions of the reconstituted Siam in 1785 and 1786 failed (Konbaung dynasty page); no border moved.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1788)
wars.outcome: Burmese defensive victory: Siam tried to capture Tavoy and reclaim the Tenasserim coast and failed; no ground changed hands.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1792-1794)
wars.outcome: Burmese defensive victory: Tavoy's governor defected to Siam in March 1792 and Siam held Tavoy and Mergui; the Siamese were defeated at Tavoy in January 1794 and Mergui returned to Burma.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1797-1798)
wars.outcome: Siamese defensive victory: Burma invaded Lan Na and besieged Chiang Mai; Kawila asked Rama I for reinforcements; no ground changed hands.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1802-1805)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Chiang Saen, the Burmese base in Lan Na, was taken by Chiang Mai forces in 1804.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1809-1812)
wars.outcome: Siamese defensive victory: Burma's attempts to capture Junk Ceylon (Thalang) were repelled in 1810 and 1812; no ground changed hands.

certainty.note: No treaty line: the Kaungton settlement of 1769 left the Yunnan border undemarcated, the Shan and Lan Na frontiers are tributary margins, and the Tenasserim line to Siam is a pass line.
